subject: Decision: compliance tool renewal vs. migrate - proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compliance tool contract coming up — decision & plan needed

Team,

Our Drata subscription is up for renewal on 2026-10-31. I attached the latest renewal quote and a very high-level cost delta if we keep Drata vs. switch to TrustCenter or consolidate under an in-house evaluation approach.

Quick context:
- Current spend: ~$80k/year (net after discount).
- Controls coverage: broadly matches SOC2 in scope; we've had some gaps in continuous evidence collection for infra changes.
- Support SLA: adequate, but recent ticket slowness during the last audit added friction.

Options on the table (short):
1) Renew Drata for 12 months (fastest, lowest immediate migration risk).
2) Migrate to TrustCenter — potentially better UI and consolidated Trust Center listing; requires ~6-8 week onboarding and extra integration effort.
3) Pause renewal and run internal instrumentation pilot (6 months) to validate replacing auto evidence collection — higher risk to audits.

What I need from you by EOD Tue 2026-09-14:
- Marissa: procurement constraints and preferred procurement path (SPO terms, PO timing).
- Karthik: legal / security redlines that would affect a vendor swap; major blockers?
- Laura: CS/ops impact estimate for a 6–8 week migration window and resource needs.

I propose we do a short decision meeting next week (30m) after you send notes — I can invite the vendor reps if we want to pressure-test their timelines.

Thanks,

Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: drata_renewal_quote_2026-09-08.pdf, migration-risk-assessment-draft.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance tool contract coming up — decision & plan needed

Thanks Olga — good summary. Procurement notes:
- We can execute a PO for renewal within 2 weeks if legal signoff is clean. Finance wants final invoice before 2026-10 close to align to FY26 commitments.
- If we switch vendors, procurement needs 4–6 weeks to validate terms, SOC reports, and process the onboarding agreements. Marketplace route (e.g., cloud marketplace) could shave time but may limit negotiation leverage.

Karthik — please flag any KBA/CIA items that would force us to keep Drata for another year.

Laura — can you draft a short ops-runbook for a migration pilot? Include what telemetry we must keep live while migrating. If migration needs >0.5 FTEs for engineering it's going to be hard to absorb.

Marissa
Director, Procurement
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <pshah@trustcenter.example>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: TrustCenter proposal and gap analysis (preview)

Hi Olga — it was great to talk yesterday. Per our call I attached a concise feature-gap spreadsheet and a recommended quick-onboard package for Redwood. Highlights:
- We cover 95% of your current control mapping and have a managed integration for AWS/GCP that reduces manual evidence by ~60%.
- Typical onboarding: 4–6 weeks for a team of two (Redwood provides 1 SME + 1 infra engineer).
- Pricing: competitive with a migration credit for the first year if you commit 12 months.

I've included a suggested pilot scope: focus on automated infra evidence (5 controls) + one policy automation. If pilot is green, we can fast-track the Trust Center listing and a 12-month contract with migration credits.

Attachments (sent separately): trustcenter_feature-gap-analysis.xlsx

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Solutions — TrustCenter
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@drata.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Compliance tool contract coming up — decision & plan needed

Team — quick update after reviewing vendor materials and legal constraints:

Summary:
- Drata (current) submitted a renewal quote that is ~+5% on last year but includes priority onboarding credits — low migration risk.
- TrustCenter provided a strong migration package and a clear 4–6 week pilot plan; they included a feature-gap workbook which is very useful.
- Legal (Karthik): no blocking security clauses for migration, but we must preserve audit continuity and ensure immutable audit logs during any transition.
- Procurement (Marissa): timeline to switch vendors is feasible but will need a signed pilot SOW by 2026-10-07 to meet FY26 procurement windows.

Decision (proposed): run a focused 6-week pilot with TrustCenter for infra evidence automation while simultaneously issuing a trimmed 3-month renewal with Drata as a safety net (covering 2026-11 through 2027-01). This reduces audit risk while giving us an escape hatch if migration stalls.

Next steps (owners):
- Marissa: negotiate a 3-month term with Drata and route PO by 2026-09-24.
- Karthik: draft the pilot SOW template language and the audit continuity clause by 2026-09-22.
- Laura: finalize ops runbook and list of telemetry that must stay live during migration by 2026-09-22.
- Olga: coordinate kick-off meeting with TrustCenter and Drata (vendor witness) the week of 2026-09-27.

Attachments: trustcenter_feature-gap-analysis.xlsx, migration-risk-assessment-draft.docx, drata_renewal_quote_2026-09-08.pdf

Thanks — this gives us a pragmatic path that minimizes audit exposure and keeps momentum on automation.

Olga
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
